title: Zscaler's Azure Terraform package for Cloud Connector: image, VM sizes, provider constraint, examples and FIPS

prose.text: Zscaler's Azure Terraform package is a reference implementation: its modules, example roots and the zsec helper script each enforce their own defaults and checks, and those layers do not always agree with each other or with the package's own documentation. Nothing here is a Cloud Connector service limit unless a claim says so.

checks.do: Whether the Marketplace image terms were accepted in the target subscription before the first apply.
Whether the chosen VM size is in the allow-list of the module that will receive it (the VMSS module has no Standard_DS2_v2), not only the example root's list.
Whether the azurerm provider in use satisfies the modules' versions.tf, not the README range.
Whether the selected example root declares fips_enabled before relying on the zsec FIPS answer, by reading the rendered user_data for FIPS_ENABLED.

marketplace-vm-size.statement: In the Azure Marketplace deployment the instance type is Small by default and the VM size is set automatically to Standard D2ds v5, which can be changed.

ds2-vmss-fails-in-child.statement: Choosing Standard_DS2_v2 for a VMSS deployment (which zsec offers in the China regions) passes the example root's validation and then fails the VMSS module's validation. This is a defect between the package's layers; it says nothing about whether Azure or the Cloud Connector service would accept the size.
ds2-vmss-fails-in-child.conditions: Follows from the helper menu, the root and child validators at the pin; not run.

fips-variable.statement: The changelog adds a `fips_enabled` variable for enabling FIPS mode through user data, and the example roots that have it write `FIPS_ENABLED=${var.fips_enabled}` into the `[ZSCALER]` user data.

quotes: add new `fips_enabled` variable for enabling FIPS mode via userdata
userdata = <<USERDATA [ZSCALER]
FIPS_ENABLED=${var.fips_enabled}

fips-roots.statement: At the pin, `fips_enabled` and `FIPS_ENABLED` appear in `base_1cc`, `base_1cc_zpa`, `base_cc_lb`, `base_cc_lb_zpa`, `base_cc_vmss`, `base_cc_vmss_zpa`, `cc_lb` and `cc_vmss`, and in none of `base_cc_gwlb`, `base_cc_gwlb_vmss`, `base_cc_public_lb`, `base_cc_public_vmss`, `cc_gwlb`, `cc_gwlb_vmss` and `cc_public_lb` (nor `base` and `ztags_standalone`).
fips-roots.conditions: Search of each example root's variables.tf and main.tf at the pinned commit for fips_enabled and FIPS_ENABLED.

quotes: FIPS_ENABLED=${var.fips_enabled}
FIPS_ENABLED=${var.fips_enabled}

zsec-fips-prompt.statement: For every deployment type other than `base`, the `zsec` helper asks whether to enable FIPS mode and writes `TF_VAR_fips_enabled` ('True' or 'False') to .zsecrc.

quotes: Enable FIPS mode for this Cloud Connector deployment? (yes/no):
echo "export TF_VAR_fips_enabled='True'" >> .zsecrc
echo "export TF_VAR_fips_enabled='False'" >> .zsecrc

fips-noop-roots.statement: For the seven GWLB and Public LB roots, answering yes to the zsec FIPS prompt has no effect: the roots declare no `fips_enabled` input, so Terraform does not use the exported value and their user data carries no FIPS setting. This is a helper and example defect; it does not show whether the service supports FIPS on those topologies.
fips-noop-roots.conditions: Terraform ignores a TF_VAR_ environment value for which the root declares no variable; that behavior is Terraform's, not quoted from a registered source.

direct-modules-no-fips.statement: The direct VM and VMSS modules take caller-built `user_data` and declare no `fips_enabled` variable, so FIPS coverage comes from the example roots, not from the modules.
direct-modules-no-fips.conditions: Search of both direct modules' variables.tf at the pin for fips; only the user_data input is quoted.

quotes: variable "user_data" { type = string description = "Cloud Init data" }
variable "user_data" { type = string description = "Cloud Init data" }

legacy-vm-nva-help.statement: Help's Marketplace procedure, on the Tags tab, says to enable LegacyVMNVA to opt out of Microsoft Azure Network Adapter (MANA)-enabled hardware.

ex-starter.statement: `base_1cc` adds to the base deployment one Cloud Connector private subnet associated to a NAT gateway, one Cloud Connector VM, and a workload subnet UDR repointed to the Cloud Connector's service interface IP.

quotes: Additionally: Creates 1 Cloud Connector private subnet associated to a NAT Gateway; 1 Cloud Connector VM; and workload private subnet UDR repointed to service interface IP of Cloud Connector.

ex-lb.statement: `base_cc_lb` creates two Cloud Connector private subnets with two NAT gateways, two Cloud Connector VMs and a Standard Azure Load Balancer, with the workload subnet UDR routing to the load balancer frontend IP; the README calls the Standard Load Balancer Zscaler's recommended deployment method.

quotes: Additionally: Creates 2 Cloud Connector private subnets associated to a 2 NAT Gateways; 2 Cloud Connector VMs; Standard Azure Load Balancer; and workload private subnet UDR routing to the Load Balancer Frontend IP.
to load balance traffic across multiple Cloud Connectors. Zscaler's recommended deployment method is Azure Standard Load Balancer.

ex-zpa.statement: The `_zpa` greenfield variants add a Private DNS Resolver, ruleset, rules per entered domain, a virtual network link and an outbound endpoint in a dedicated outbound DNS subnet.

quotes: Private DNS Resolver, Private DNS Resolver Ruleset, Private DNS Resolver rules based on the number of domains entered, Virtual Network Link for Ruleset, and Outbound Endpoint in a dedicated Outbound DNS subnet.

Private DNS Resolver, Private DNS Resolver Ruleset, Private DNS Resolver rules based on the number of domains entered, Virtual Network Link for Ruleset, and Outbound Endpoint in a dedicated Outbound DNS subnet.

ex-vmss.statement: `base_cc_vmss` creates one or more Flexible Orchestration scale sets with scaling policies, one Function App for VMSS and a Standard Azure Load Balancer, with the workload UDR routing to the load balancer frontend IP.

quotes: Additionally: Depending on the configuration, creates 1 or more Flexible Orchestration Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS) and scaling policies for Cloud Connector in private subnet(s); and 1 function app for VMSS; Standard Azure Load Balancer; and workload private subnet UDR routing to the Load Balancer Frontend IP.

ex-gwlb.statement: `base_cc_gwlb` and `cc_gwlb` deploy Cloud Connectors with an Azure Gateway Load Balancer for transparent inline traffic inspection, and `base_cc_gwlb_vmss` and `cc_gwlb_vmss` add Virtual Machine Scale Sets.

quotes: Use the [**Starter Deployment Template with Gateway Load Balancer**](examples/base_cc_gwlb) to deploy your Cloud Connectors in a new resource group and virtual network with an Azure Gateway Load Balancer for transparent inline traffic inspection.
Use the [**Starter Deployment Template with Gateway Load Balancer and VMSS**](examples/base_cc_gwlb_vmss)

Use the [**Custom Deployment template with Gateway Load Balancer**](examples/cc_gwlb) to deploy your Cloud Connectors in a new or existing VNet with an Azure Gateway Load Balancer for transparent inline traffic inspection.
Use the [**Custom Deployment template with Gateway Load Balancer and VMSS**](examples/cc_gwlb_vmss)

ex-public-lb.statement: `base_cc_public_lb` fronts the Cloud Connectors with an Azure Standard Public Load Balancer for inbound traffic distribution (for example fwd ZIA DNAT), implementing a routed PLB to Cloud Connector to ILB ingress topology; `base_cc_public_vmss` does the same with scale sets.

quotes: fronted by an Azure Standard Public Load Balancer for inbound traffic distribution (e.g. `fwd ZIA` DNAT use cases).
Use the [**Starter Deployment Template with Public Load Balancer and VMSS**](examples/base_cc_public_vmss)
implementing the **routed-mode PLB → CC → ILB ingress topology** for ZIA inspection.

ex-brownfield.statement: `cc_lb` and `cc_vmss` are intended for brownfield/production use, deploying into a new or existing VNet with at least one Cloud Connector subnet and NAT gateway and a Standard Azure Load Balancer (`cc_vmss` adds scale sets and a Function App), with optional Private DNS Resolver resources per `zpa_enabled`.

quotes: This deployment type is intended for brownfield/production purposes.
at least 1 Cloud Connector private subnet; at least 1 NAT Gateway with Public IP Address association to the Cloud Connector subnets;
at least 1 Virtual Machine Scale Set (VMSS); and 1 function app for VMSS;
to deploy your Cloud Connector in a new or existing VNet and load balance traffic across multiple Cloud Connectors.
Optional Azure Private DNS Resolver resource creation per variable zpa_enabled.

image-terms-error.title: Failure when Marketplace image terms are not accepted
image-terms-error.detail: Unverified legacy statement: skipping the image-terms acceptance produces an Azure Resource Manager error rather than a Zscaler error, which is easy to misdiagnose. The package README requires the acceptance but does not show the failure.
image-terms-error.blocks: recognizing a first-deploy failure caused by unaccepted terms

arm-marketplace-path.title: ARM templates behind the Marketplace deployment
arm-marketplace-path.detail: Unverified legacy statement: ARM templates exist as the Azure Marketplace wizard path but are not separately published as a standalone repository. The captured sources describe the Marketplace application and the Terraform repository as the two methods and say nothing about ARM templates.
arm-marketplace-path.blocks: telling an operator whether an ARM or Bicep template is available for Azure Cloud Connector
